summary: The diff implements %StringIteratorPrototype%.next in the one in-scope file. The receiver is brand-checked first and throws a TypeError otherwise. A completed iterator (string = None) returns { value: undefined, done: true }. Otherwise it returns the next code point as a substring and advances position, and at the end it marks the iterator completed. The local code_point_unit_count helper matches CodePointAt (§6.1.5.1) step by step, including lone and trailing surrogates and the end-of-string case. Nothing is special-cased, no errors are swallowed, and the only observable operations are the brand check and the iterator result creation. The two lint flags are .expect() calls after a successful native() lookup with no intervening state change, so they are not reachable panics. They are a style issue, not a defect.
notes_for_next_attempt: Optional cleanups, not blockers. (1) next.rs lines ~43 and ~60: the two .expect("a String Iterator") calls after a successful agent.native::<StringIterator>(it) check are unreachable, but the lint flags them. Consider taking a single native_mut borrow up front and mutating through it, which removes the expect. (2) The ticket says to use kahvi_core::ops rather than re-implementing. The local code_point_unit_count helper says no shared CodePointAt helper exists. Please confirm that against ops before merging, and if one exists, use it. (3) The step labels in the comments (e.g. "Closure step 4.a/4.c/4.d") are cosmetic. Check them against the pinned spec text if you want them exact.
